Answer Part 2: Spec DD (Specification-Driven Development)

Specification link: docs/lab-03/specification.md. Written upfront as Issue 1 before implementation began.

2.1 Sprint Goal & Stakeholder Interpretation

Sprint Goal: Replace the development requester selector with secure email/password authentication, implement session-based identity across all routes, introduce operational IT Staff ticketing workflows (queue, claim/reassign, priority, status transitions, public comments, internal notes), and add a minimalist Administrator screen for user account management.

Stakeholder Interpretation: Move from an unauthenticated prototype to a secure multi-role system where Requesters, IT Staff, and Administrators operate with distinct, server-enforced boundaries. Server-side validation must be authoritative; hiding UI buttons does not constitute authorization.

2.2 Functional Requirements (FR-01 to FR-12)

  • FR-01: Authentication — Authenticate with email and password, establishing an HTTP-only session cookie.
  • FR-02: Mandatory Password Change — Users with mustChangePassword = true cannot reach normal screens until a valid password is saved.
  • FR-03: Current User & Logout — GET /api/auth/me returns session info; POST /api/auth/logout invalidates session.
  • FR-04: Session-Based Requester Scoping — All ticket/attachment endpoints authorize using req.session.userId.
  • FR-05: Requester Comments & Advisory Flag — Requesters can post Public Comments and mark "Problem Appears Resolved".
  • FR-06: IT Staff Ticket Queue — Paginated, searchable, filterable, and sortable queue covering all system tickets.
  • FR-07: Claim & Reassign — IT Staff can claim unassigned tickets or reassign ownership to another active IT Staff member.
  • FR-08: IT Priority & Status Transitions — IT Staff can adjust IT Priority and execute permitted status transitions.
  • FR-09: Public Comments vs Internal Notes — Public Comments shared with requester; Internal Notes restricted to IT Staff/Admin.
  • FR-10: Administrator User Management — List, search, role-filter, create user, edit details, and reset initial password.
  • FR-11: Administrator Safety Guards — Prevent self-deactivation and prevent removal of the last active Administrator.
  • FR-12: Role-Aware App Shell — Header dynamically displays authenticated user, role badge, and role-permitted navigation links.

  2. Authentication Foundation (Issue 2):
    Prompt: "Do Issue 2 and tell me what to ADD, not the whole zip. Use bcryptjs for cross-platform compatibility."
  3. Migration Error Recovery:
    Prompt: "Prisma migration failure: P3006 / P1014 duplicate table Requester. How to safely consolidate migrations without data loss?"
  4. Token-Efficient File Delivery:
    Prompt: "Give me only the files that changed to avoid token truncation and copy-paste errors."
  5. Requester Regression & Public Comments (Issue 3):
    Prompt: "Switch the Lab 2 endpoints to the authenticated session and add Public Comments and Problem Appears Resolved action."
  6. IT Staff Ticket Queue (Issue 4):
    Prompt: "Implement the IT Staff Ticket Queue with multi-parameter filtering (status, priority, owner), search, and pagination."
  7. Staff Ticket Detail & Administrator Management (Issues 5 & 6):
    Prompt: "Build Staff Ticket Detail (claim, reassign, priority, internal notes) and User Management (CRUD, self-deactivation guard, last admin guard)."
  8. Integration QA & Playwright Suites (Issue 7):
    Prompt: "Do the QA and E2E Issue. Migrate Lab 2 Playwright specs to real login and capture responsive screenshots at 3 viewports."

4.2 My Reflection

Specification Agent: Generating the comprehensive specification first (authorization matrix, transition matrix, numbered BR rules, and acceptance criteria) made implementation structured and verifiable. Every test could be traced directly to an Acceptance Criterion. The only flaw was process discipline: Issue 1 was committed directly to staging without an initial PR.

Coding Agent: The coding agent was fast and made sound architectural choices (server-side authorization, HTTP-only session cookies, no client-supplied IDs). However, it struggled where it could not execute commands directly: migrations, local database nuances, and test executions. Running test suites locally after every single issue was crucial to catching minor test mock discrepancies and ensuring 100% real-world stability.

Answer Part 5: Working Login and Password Change UI

5.1 Authentication Features & Security Policy

  • Dual-Field Login: Email and password fields with busy loading state and inline error banner.
  • Safe Failure Feedback: Generic "Invalid email or password" returned for unknown emails, bad passwords, and inactive accounts (BR-01, BR-02), preventing account enumeration attacks.
  • Mandatory First Password Change: Users with mustChangePassword: true are intercepted immediately and redirected to the password change screen before any application data is exposed.
  • Password Policy Enforcement: Minimum 8 characters, at least one letter and one number, and confirmation matching.
  • Session Invalidation: Logout completely clears the session cookie and prevents subsequent back-button navigation.

Answer Part 6: Working IT Staff Ticket Queue UI

6.1 Operational Queue Capabilities

  • Search & Multi-Parameter Filters: Text search across ticket number and summary; dropdown filters for Status, IT Priority, and Ticket Owner.
  • Sorting & Pagination: Sortable table columns with clean server-side pagination metadata (showing range, total count, prev/next controls).
  • Status & Priority Badges: Visual pills using Zen Green color coding paired with text labels for accessibility.
  • Clear Ownership Indication: Assigned staff member name displayed or distinct "Unassigned" chip.
  • Empty & No-Results State: Clean empty state illustration with a "Clear Filters" button when queries match zero tickets.

Answer Part 7: Working IT Staff Ticket Detail UI

7.1 Operational Actions & Communication Channels

  • Atomic Claim: Unassigned tickets feature a prominent "Claim Ticket" button that assigns the ticket to the current staff user and updates status from NEW to OPEN.
  • Reassignment: Staff can reassign ticket ownership to any active IT Staff member via dropdown.
  • Independent IT Priority: Staff can adjust IT Priority without overwriting the Requester's original Requested Priority.
  • Status Transition Controls: Status dropdown presents only valid transitions per the matrix; invalid requests are blocked with HTTP 400.
  • Public Comments vs. Internal Notes:
    • Public Comments: Shared conversation visible to both Requester and IT Staff (rendered in green card containers).
    • Internal Notes: Private operational notes visible exclusively to IT Staff and Administrators (rendered in distinct amber containers). Requesters attempting to query notes receive 403 Forbidden.
  • Problem Appears Resolved Flag: When a requester marks the advisory flag, a banner alerts staff. Resolving the ticket automatically resets the flag.

Answer Part 8: Working Administrator User Management UI

8.1 User Management Screen & Safety Guards

  • User Directory: Clean table listing all users with Name, Email, Role badge, Status (Active/Inactive), and Edit action.
  • Search & Role Filter: Live search by user name or email address, with quick role filtering.
  • Create User Modal: Form with name, email, role selection, active toggle, and generated compliant initial password.
  • Duplicate Email Prevention: Case-insensitive duplicate check rejects duplicates with clear field-level validation errors (HTTP 400).
  • Safety Rules (BR-18, BR-19):
    • An Administrator cannot deactivate their own active account.
    • The system blocks deactivating or changing the role of the last active Administrator (protected in unit test admin-safety.unit.test.ts).
    • Soft deactivation is used instead of user deletion to preserve ticket history and audit integrity.
  • Password Reset: Administrators can generate a new temporary password for any user; the user's existing session is immediately invalidated, forcing a password change on next login.

Answer Part 9: Zen Green UI and Responsive Evidence

9.1 Zen Green UI Tokens & Conventions

Lab 3 preserves and extends the Zen Green design system established in Lab 2:

  • Palette: Primary Forest Green (#006B3C), Accent Deep Emerald (#2d6a4f), Background Soft Mint (#EEF2EF), Card White (#ffffff), Border Mint (#d8f3dc).
  • Semantic Distinctions: Public Comments in soft green containers (#e8f5e9); Internal Notes in distinct soft amber containers (#fef3c7) with amber border (#f59e0b).
  • Role-Aware Header: App shell shows the user's name and role pill with distinct styling (Requester: blue-green, IT Staff: emerald, Administrator: purple-slate).
